items.action: audit clock enablement by resolving the DTB's flat clock cells against the driver's registered IDs, per provider domain
items.reason: 'the driver compiles and the symbol is on' says nothing about whether the provider can answer the board. Three tool bugs had to be fixed to make the number trustworthy, each of which would have produced a false all-clear or a false alarm: dtc -O dts prefixes nodes with their label ('pericfg: pericfg@10003000 {'), so a name-only regex lost the providers and made every reference look dangling; '#clock-cells' needs '#' in the property regex; multi-string compatibles print as one quoted string separated by \0 and must be split. Domain attribution also has to include mux/divider/factor tables, not just *_clks[], or topckgen reads as 5/65 registered when it is 65/65.

Vendor MT6768 PMIC-wrap map agrees with mainline's mt8183 table on all 43 comparable registers (0 differing) and with mt6765 on only 6 of 20 (RDDMY/HARB_HPRIO/MAN_CMD/WACS0_EN/INIT_DONE2/TIMER_EN/DCM all shifted). Offsets for every register pwrap_mt8183_init_soc_specific() writes were checked individually. MT6768 also has P2P/MD32 masters in its DTB, so that init applies.

Taken from the vendor's own MT6768 init (pwrap_hal.c:901,913) instead of MT8183's 0x3fa75/0xeef7ffff: the arbiter mask differs in bit 4 (which bus masters may reach the PMIC), so reusing MT8183's value would have been an invention with real consequences.

items.action: port: mt6358-regulator per-rdev of_node via of_regulator_match()

Match names are the driver's own desc.name strings; 41/41 of them exist as children in this DTB (42 children, ldo_va09 unmatched). of_regulator_match() returns a count and tolerates absent children, so other MT6358 boards keep prior behaviour.
